index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a comparative visualization of two distinct architectural configurations labeled 'Dense' and 'Sparse', separated by a vertical dashed line. The global layout is horizontally divided into two symmetric panels, each illustrating a different connectivity pattern between a central model component and a set of input or latent variables.

In both panels, the topmost node is a green circle labeled 'MT', representing a central model or transformer component. Below this, five circular nodes are arranged horizontally, labeled z₁ through z₅, representing individual latent variables or data points. These lower nodes are uniformly styled with black outlines and black text, contrasting with the green 'MT' node.

In the 'Dense' panel on the left, the 'MT' node connects via thick gray lines to all five z nodes (z₁ to z₅), indicating full connectivity where the model interacts with every latent variable. This suggests a dense interaction pattern, typical of fully connected architectures.

In contrast, the 'Sparse' panel on the right shows the 'MT' node connected by a single thick gray line only to z₃, while the other four z nodes (z₁, z₂, z₄, z₅) remain unconnected. This illustrates a sparse interaction pattern, where the model selectively engages with only one latent variable out of the set.

The visual distinction emphasizes the difference in computational efficiency and information flow: dense implies comprehensive processing of all inputs, whereas sparse implies selective or localized processing. No additional text, equations, or annotations are present beyond the labels and structural connections. The figure serves to visually contrast dense versus sparse modeling strategies in the context of the MT component's interaction with latent variables.
